findings.finding: The bar Ceres itself publishes -- eight analysts, FY2026e revenue GBP60.0m and Adj. EBITDA of POSITIVE GBP1.0m -- sits GBP15m above the 'approximately GBP45m' of contracted 2026 revenue the company stated on 26 March 2026, and in the six months since Ceres has announced no new manufacturing-licence partner at all (the last was Weichai, 5 November 2025); the Centrica and Delta/Centrica partnerships of 26 March and 30 April 2026 disclose no licence fee, no revenue value and no recognition timing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ceres is punished hard when the revenue outlook is trimmed: Trading update 24 Jan 2024 -15.10%, Final results 21 Mar 2025 -7.97%, and the last interims on 26 Sep 2025, at which FY2025 revenue was guided to 'around GBP32 million', -8.77%. All three are observed_rns rows in the sealed baseline. The one large positive results reaction, +26.57% on 27 Sep 2024, came in a half where a signed licence (Delta, GBP43m staged) was already funding the number.

findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I have sized it accordingly. If it were fully priced the sell-side targets would not still be 920p (Jefferies, 10 June 2026) and 980p (Berenberg, May 2026) against a 415p spot, and the company would not still be publishing a breakeven-EBITDA 2026 on its own website five months after the contracted figure was set GBP15m lower. What IS priced is the direction -- a 13.3% short base is paid to hold exactly this view -- which is why this is -2.5 and not -6.
findings.independence: Simply Wall St's read of the same post-FY25 revision, eight analysts cutting FY2026 revenue from GBP63.6m to GBP60.0m while raising the loss per share to GBP0.066: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analysts-lowered-expectations-ceres-power-130138399.html

findings.finding: Ceres told the market in the Weichai licence RNS that the licence fees land in FY2026, on terms 'consistent with previous Ceres manufacturing licensing agreements' -- and the previous one, Delta Electronics in January 2024, was GBP43m staged with about half recognised in year one. Weichai then launched its CE-certified, Ceres-based SOFC system on 18 February 2026 with over 30,000 hours of cumulative operation, so the technology-transfer milestones that trigger those fees are running. That makes H1 2026 revenue likely to be UP against H1 2025's GBP21.1m, into a domestic narrative ('falling revenue', 'two fundraisings') and a short thesis that both assume the opposite.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The half in which the previous manufacturing licence fee was recognised was H1 2024: revenue GBP28.5m against GBP12-13m the year before, and the 27 Sep 2024 interims moved +26.57%, the largest reaction in the twelve observed_rns rows in the baseline. The mirror case is H1 2025, the half with no new licence: revenue fell 26% to GBP21.1m and the print moved -8.77%. This line has the widest realised dispersion of any at this name.
findings.original_quote: Given the timing of the agreement, revenue recognition for the licence fees are likely to be booked in FY26 so 2025 Group revenues will remain as previously guided. ... licence fees, milestones and royalties are consistent with previous Ceres manufacturing licensing agreements.
findings.why_not_priced: The sentence is one clause in a thirteen-month-old RNS and it never reached the wire copy: the English-language coverage of Ceres in 2026 is about the AI-datacentre narrative, the June placing and the 50% drawdown, and the domestic retail write-ups (ABC Money, 30 July 2026) frame the name as 'falling revenue' full stop. If the market held the licence-phasing point, a name whose contracted 2026 revenue is 38% above its 2025 actual would not be trading 27% below its own June placing price with the disclosed short doubling. Note this does NOT lift FY2026 to the GBP60m bar -- Weichai is already inside the GBP45m contracted -- which is why it coexists with the finding above rather than contradicting it.
findings.independence: Weichai's CE-certification launch of the Ceres-based system, 18 February 2026, is the physical milestone behind the fee, reported independently of Ceres: https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-partner-weichai-launches-stationary-power-sofc-system-at-ceremony-to-mark-its-ce-certification-with-tuev-sued/

findings.finding: Ceres disclosed in the 9 June 2026 placing RNS that it held 'unaudited cash and short-term investments of GBP78.7 million as of 31 May 2026' against GBP83.3m at 31 December 2025 -- an outflow of only GBP4.6m in five months, roughly half the FY2025 run-rate (net cash used in operating activities GBP20.1m; adjusted EBITDA loss GBP32.5m) -- and then raised GBP103m gross at 570p. So the 30 June 2026 balance sheet should carry roughly GBP175m of net cash and investments, about 20% of the GBP890m market capitalisation and about GBP100m above the FY2026e cash figure the company's own consensus page still shows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing news at this name has been read both ways: the placing itself was met with a rise on admission (12 June 2026) because insiders subscribed and the CEO retained his shares, but the stock then fell from 570p to 362p by 1 September as the domestic press rolled the raise into a dilution-and-burn story. The FY2025 results on 26 Mar 2026 led with GBP83.3m of cash and a reduced outflow and moved +6.67%.
findings.original_quote: unaudited cash and short-term investments of GBP78.7 million as of 31 May 2026 ... strengthen the balance sheet for growth, support partner scale-up, and enable selective investment in key intellectual property and component supply facilities
findings.why_not_priced: Financing is a question here and the answer is a ramp, not distress: the money buys IP and a component supply facility, and three independent counterparties corroborate the ramp -- Delta is building at Tainan for production start by end-2026, Weichai has a CE-certified system, and Doosan signed a KRW108.7bn (c.GBP60m) SOFC stack export order with Reverion on 6 August 2026. The domestic read is the opposite: ABC Money on 30 July 2026 wrote that 'a further fundraising ... cannot be ruled out'. The arithmetic -- GBP4.6m of burn in five months -- was never in a headline; it sat in the ninth paragraph of a placing announcement that the market read for the price and the discount.
findings.independence: The FY2025 results give the other half of the subtraction, 'Net cash and investments 83,272' and 'Net cash used in operating activities (20,070)': https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf . The Doosan/Reverion order that corroborates the ramp: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ceres-power-holdings--cwr/doosan-fuel-cell-sofc-order-with-reverion-gmbh/9708112

findings.finding: Ceres is the fifth most heavily shorted stock in the entire UK disclosed register -- 13.3% of shares outstanding at position date 18/09/2026, out of 423 issuers -- and the position was still being added to through an 11% rally (13.21% at 16/09 in the sealed baseline, 13.3% at 18/09 on the file fetched 2026-09-22). On 214.5m shares (BlackRock's TR-1 of 28 July 2026 pins 12,548,472 shares at 5.85%) that is 28.5m shares short against a 20-day median volume of 1.64m, or 17.4 days to cover, into a one-session event on a name with 79% 20-day realised volatility and no daily price limit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's twelve observed reactions have a median absolute move of 6.06% and a maximum of +26.57%, and the sealed lean already carries +3.0 for squeeze against -2.0 for building. What the lean cannot carry is the cover ratio: at 17.4 days the marginal short cannot exit into a 07:00 RNS, which is the mechanism behind the two US names in this repo's record that squeezed more than 20% from 18% and 23% of float.
findings.why_not_priced: The level is in the baseline; the three things that are not are (a) the rank -- fifth of 423, which no summary of this name states, (b) the cover ratio of 17.4 sessions, which needs the share count out of a TR-1 and the volume out of the tape, and (c) that the FCA's per-holder file is frozen at 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026', where these same holders summed to roughly 6.6%, so the doubling since July is invisible at holder level and nobody can see who is short. If the squeeze risk were priced, the December 2025 Grizzly short report would not still be the top organic search result for this company's commercial prospects while the sell-side sits at 920-980p.
findings.independence: The frozen per-holder file that shows the same names at roughly half the current aggregate: https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx (only sheet: 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026'; last Ceres row Marshall Wace 1.34% at 08/07/2026)

findings.finding: The royalty line -- the single number the December 2025 Grizzly Research short report says will never materialise -- will almost certainly still be immaterial in H1 2026: FY2025 royalties were GBP110k on total revenue of GBP32.6m, Ceres' own FY2025 framing is that royalties 'scale from 2027', and its only royalty-paying licensee, Doosan Fuel Cell, reported H1 2026 revenue of KRW189.1bn against KRW454.8bn a year earlier with a KRW52.2bn operating loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first-ever royalty disclosure, in the FY2025 results of 26 Mar 2026, moved the stock +6.67% -- but that RNS was followed two minutes later by 'Ceres and Centrica sign a strategic partnership' at 07:02, so the royalty number itself has never been priced alone at this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Honestly, it mostly IS priced -- this is the shorts' core claim and 13.3% of the register is paid to hold it -- which is why it is sized at -0.5 rather than -3. It is also a weak proxy in the direction that cuts against me: Doosan's revenue fall is its legacy PAFC business, while its SOFC line went the other way (first overseas stack export, a KRW108.7bn Reverion order, a new 50MW factory). I keep it only because the royalty line is the marquee number in this print and a reader should see it sized rather than omitted.
findings.independence: Ceres' own FY2025 statement that royalties scale from 2027 and that FY2025 royalties were GBP110k: https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf ; the short thesis it restates: https://grizzlyreports.com/ceres/ (11 December 2025)

outside_window.finding: Delta Electronics is due to start pilot production of Ceres-based SOFC at Tainan 'by the end of 2026', which is the trigger for the next royalty step-up; nothing about it resolves on 23 September.

The RFC Power / Certain Energy spin-out completed on 26 August 2026 (Ceres retains c.37% plus a revenue share, contributed GBP1m cash and took GBP1.5m of equity for in-kind engineering) is a post-balance-sheet event: any deconsolidation gain lands in H2 2026, not in the half being reported.
Doosan's KRW108.7bn (c.GBP60m) SOFC stack supply contract with Reverion, announced 6 August 2026, converts to Ceres royalties only as stacks ship; no part of it is in the half being reported.

searched_and_found_nothing: A company-published H1 2026 revenue or EBITDA expectation: none exists. Ceres has issued no trading update since the FY2025 results, and the 3 Sep 2026 Notice of Interim Results carries no numbers. The 9 June placing RNS carries a cash figure but, unusually for a UK placing, no trading commentary at all.

A quantified licence fee for Weichai: the 5 Nov 2025 RNS says only 'consistent with previous Ceres manufacturing licensing agreements' and names no figure, so the Delta GBP43m read-across is an inference and is sized as one.

Any commercial value attached to the Centrica partnership (26 Mar 2026) or the Delta/Centrica infrastructure partnership (30 Apr 2026): both RNSs disclose no licence fee, no revenue and no recognition timing.

A cause for the +15.48% five-day run-up in Ceres' own filings: there has been no RNS since 3 September 2026. The nearest explanation is sector flow -- FuelCell Energy +13%, Plug +7%, Bloom +3% on 17 Sep on a US House bill shifting data-centre power costs to operators, and Bloom's S&P 500 entry on 21 Sep -- which is a hypothesis about transmission, not a company fact, so I have not made a finding of it.
Investegate's UK short-positions page returns no per-company data to either curl or WebFetch; I used the FCA files directly instead.

Sharecast, Proactive Investors and the Investors' Chronicle are recorded in researcher_europe/LESSONS.md as 403 to both tools; I routed around them rather than spending calls, and their Ceres URLs surfaced in search results only.

The Ceres FY2025 and H1 2025 results PDFs on ceres.tech are font-subset PDFs that eu_pdftext.py reads only partially (H1 2025 returned no usable text); the H1 2025 line items quoted here come from the Investegate/press record, not from the PDF, and are marked as such.
baseline_tension: It cuts against the lean in composition and agrees with it in sign: the sealed lean is +0.909 built from a squeeze credit net of a short-building debit, and my strongest finding is that the building is itself the fuel (17.4 days to cover, 5th of 423) -- but the 20-day run-up of only +1.82% hides a +15.48% five-day run on sector flow, so the entry price has already taken part of the relief case and my emitted number is a point below the sum of my findings because of it.

The 9 June placing RNS text gave 'unaudited cash and short-term investments of GBP78.7 million as of 31 May 2026', which against GBP83.3m at 31 Dec 2025 is GBP4.6m of burn in five months -- half the FY2025 run-rate. Settled the session from the issuer's own RNS rather than the vendor default: 'Notice of Interim Results', Investegate, 03 Sep 2026 07:00, plus every prior Ceres results RNS stamped 07:00 in the company archive.
Confirmed there has been no RNS of any kind since 3 September 2026, which is what makes the +15.48% five-day run-up attributable to sector flow and not to leakage.
Raised expected_move from +1.0 to +2.0 and print_vs_bar from -8.0 to -10.0 on the above.
lessons_applied: 'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with' plus 'a narrow proxy loses to a broad series': my Doosan/royalty finding was both the shorts' own published thesis and a proxy (Doosan group revenue, mostly legacy PAFC) that contradicts the narrower SOFC series it is meant to stand for. Cut from -1.0 to -0.5 and the why_not_priced rewritten to say so rather than to claim an edge.

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error' and 'the tail is intact' (UK maximum 42%, no price limit): this name's own distribution is a 6.06% median absolute move with a +26.57% observation and 79% realised vol, so I widened impact_high on the positioning finding to +9.0 and on the licence-phasing finding to +5.0, and raised expected_move from +2.0 to +2.5.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number': my baseline_tension says the +15.48% five-day run-up has taken part of the case, so expected_move is held at +2.5 against a finding sum of +3.5 -- one full point below, and the conviction_note says which point and why.

'Keep findings inside the exit window': moved the Delta Tainan end-2026 production start, the RFC Power/Certain Energy deconsolidation gain and the Doosan/Reverion royalty conversion out of findings and into outside_window, sized and sourced. None of them resolves on 23 September.

'Financing is a question, not a verdict': kept the placing finding positive but rewrote it to state what the money buys (IP plus a component supply facility) and to name the three counterparty datapoints that corroborate a ramp rather than distress.

'Two findings resting on one document are one finding': the guidance finding and the cash finding both touch the consensus page, so the cash finding is re-based on the placing RNS's GBP78.7m as its load-bearing number and the overlap is stated in its independence field.
'The session is the single most load-bearing field': confirmed bmo from the issuer's own Notice of Interim Results before sizing, as instructed, rather than accepting session_unresolved.
